title: Basic Concepts of Chemistry & Stoichiometry
notes: **Mole:** the amount of substance containing as many particles (atoms, molecules, ions) as there are atoms in exactly 12 g of carbon-12. One mole = **6.022 × 10²³** particles (Avogadro's number, N_A).
**Molar mass:** mass of one mole of a substance in grams; numerically equal to its molecular/atomic weight. n = given mass / molar mass.
**Laws of chemical combination:** law of conservation of mass, law of definite (constant) proportions, law of multiple proportions and Gay-Lussac's law of gaseous volumes.
**Empirical formula** gives the simplest whole-number ratio of atoms; **molecular formula** = n × empirical formula where n = molecular mass / empirical formula mass.
**Limiting reagent:** the reactant that is completely consumed first and therefore limits the amount of product formed.
